question: Confirmation: Keith Sonderling, of F.L., to be Secretary of Labor
plain_language: This vote confirms Keith Sonderling of Florida as Secretary of Labor. A Yea confirms him. A Nay rejects the nomination.

question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Keith Sonderling to be Secretary of Labor
plain_language: This vote would end debate on confirming Keith Sonderling of Florida as Secretary of Labor. A Yea limits debate so the Senate can move to a confirmation vote. A Nay keeps debate open.

question: Booker Amdt. No. 6835 — To establish certain standards with respect to coaches of varsity sports teams.
plain_language: This amendment would have let coaches move between four-year colleges under transfer rules like those for athletes, and it would have voided a coach's endorsement deal unless the pay matched similar non-coaches and had a real business purpose. A Yea would have added those rules. A Nay rejected them.

question: Booker Amdt. No. 6805 — To increase the limitation on funding for post-eligibility insurance and catastrophic injury for student athletes.
plain_language: This amendment would have capped a student-athlete insurance and catastrophic-injury fund at $200 million and required major conferences and an athletic association to cover any amount above $100 million. A Yea would have set that cap. A Nay rejected it.

question: Kennedy Amdt. No. 6760 — To limit price increases for college athletics tickets.
plain_language: This amendment would have barred colleges, conferences, and athletic associations from raising ticket prices for a sport by more than 4 percent from the prior academic year. A Yea would have added that cap. A Nay rejected it.

question: Paul Amdt. No. 6758 — To improve the bill.
plain_language: This amendment would have replaced the college-sports bill with the Collegiate Sports Integrity Act, which centers on an antitrust exemption for athletic conferences and associations. A Yea would have made that swap. A Nay rejected it.

question: Baldwin Amdt. No. 6828 — To modify the provision relating to the relationship of this Act to existing law.
plain_language: This amendment rewrites the college-sports bill's preemption section so states generally cannot set conflicting rules on athlete publicity pay, transfers, or certain eligibility, while keeping state civil-rights, contract, privacy, and similar laws unless they conflict. A Yea adopts that text. A Nay rejects it.

question: H. Con. Res. 89 — A concurrent resolution directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
plain_language: This House resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea would agree to that direction. A Nay rejects the resolution.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

question: Amdt. No. 6776 — In the nature of a substitute.
plain_language: This substitute rewrites the college-sports bill as the Protect College Sports Act, covering athlete publicity rights, agents, medical coverage, transfers, and college-sports broadcasts. A Yea adopts that rewrite. A Nay would have left the earlier text.

question: Motion to Table Budd Amdt. No. 6747 — To strike section 2019.
plain_language: An amendment would have deleted section 2019 of the stopgap, which until December 11, 2026 narrows which Agricultural Marketing Act products are covered by changes in Public Law 119-37. This vote was to table that deletion. A Yea kills the deletion and keeps section 2019; a Nay would have left it pending.

question: H.R. 5334, as amended — An act to impose sanctions and other measures with respect to the Russian Federation, as championed by the late Senator Lindsey O. Graham, and for other purposes.
plain_language: As rewritten, this bill imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea passes that Senate version. A Nay votes against passage.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

question: Paul Amdt. No. 6715 — To strike the provision relating to duties on countries that purchase Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas or facilitate sanctions evasion.
plain_language: This amendment would replace sections 113 through 117 of the Russia-sanctions text with exceptions for humanitarian goods, intelligence and law-enforcement work, certain treaty obligations, civilian nuclear cooperation, and some space launches, plus rules for waiving or ending sanctions. A Yea adopts that replacement. A Nay rejects it.

question: S. Res. 817 — An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
plain_language: This resolution lets the Senate take up a batch of nominations together instead of one by one, covering executive jobs, judges, ambassadors, and similar posts. A Yea agrees to that group procedure. A Nay does not.
